_note: Run these against a sandbox org, never production: eval 4 starts an action run, which writes to whatever system the action is connected to. Fixture: table Deals has an action column `sync_to_erp` whose `config.input` maps `{{col_amount}}` and `{{col_owner_email}}`; `col_owner_email` reads from a stream `model_stream_<Owners table id with - as _>___local`. Two FAILED runs of that column exist. The newer one (object 'Acme renewal') is fully explained by its own result: the target system rejected the credentials, `error.isUnrecoverable` is true. The older one (object 'Globex expansion') failed with 'Please enter value(s) for: Owner email', and its `input` has an empty value under `col_owner_email`. The org has error instructions at two breadths, both returned by `errorInstructions` on that action: the integration-level text says fixes to owner data are made in the CRM and reach RevOS with the next sync within 1-2 hours; the action-level text maps 'Please enter value(s) for: Owner email' to 'the deal owner has no email in the CRM'.

evals.prompt: One of our action runs failed recently. Find it and tell me why.
evals.expected_output: Lists failed runs newest first, reads the newest one and the organization's error instructions for its action, and answers from those: the target system rejected the credentials, which is permanent, so re-running unchanged won't help. Doesn't read the table or the mapping, because the run's own result already names the cause.
expectations: Read action-runs (list and/or get) before answering
Read errorInstructions on the failed run's action before answering
Did not read the tables resource
Made at most 6 api_read calls
Reply names rejected credentials as the cause, quoting or closely following metadata.error.message
Reply does not suggest simply re-running the action unchanged

evals.prompt: Take the failed run for Globex expansion. For each column that feeds that action, tell me which table the value ultimately comes from.
evals.expected_output: Reads the run, then the table named by the run's modelId, finds the action column by columnId and reads its config.input placeholders to get the feeding columns. Decodes the `model_stream_…___local` streamId of the owner-email column into the Owners table's id and names that table; says the amount column comes from the Deals table's own source.
expectations: Read the table whose id is the run's modelId
Named exactly the columns referenced by {{…}} placeholders in the action column's config.input as the ones feeding the action
Identified the Owners table (by id or name) as the source of the owner-email column
Did not guess a source table for the column that reads the table's own stream

evals.prompt: Why didn't Globex expansion sync, and what should I do about it?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the empty owner email from the run's input and the mapping, then reads the organization's own instructions for the run's action — one `errorInstructions` read, which carries both the integration-level and the action-level text — before recommending. The answer uses their cause (the deal owner has no email in the CRM) and their resolution (fix it in the CRM; it reaches RevOS with the next sync within 1-2 hours), and says the fault is upstream data rather than the mapping.
expectations: Called api_read on actions with method errorInstructions and the run's actionId as id
Reply says the deal owner's email is missing in the CRM
Reply says the fix is made in the CRM and arrives with the next sync (1-2 hours)
Reply does not propose changing the column mapping

evals.prompt: I've fixed the owner email for Globex expansion. Run the sync for that deal again.
evals.expected_output: Starts one run with tableId, columnId and objectIds taken from the failed run (objectIds has exactly that one row), reports that it was queued, and follows it by parentId. Mentions that a fix made in the CRM only helps once it has synced into RevOS.
expectations: Exactly one api_write on action-runs
Its data has tableId = the run's modelId and columnId = the run's columnId
Its data has objectIds with exactly one id, the run's objectId
The body is under `data`
Listed action-runs filtered by the returned parentId, or told the user how the run will be followed

evals.prompt: Run the ERP sync on the Deals table.
evals.expected_output: Doesn't start a run for the whole table on its own reading of the request. Finds the action column, works out how many rows the default view covers or says it would be every row in it, and asks the user to confirm running all of them (or to name the rows) before any api_write.
expectations: No api_write on action-runs before the user confirms the scope
Reply states that without specific rows the run covers every row in the table's default view
Reply asks the user to confirm or narrow the scope
